scorer_isolation.note: Rust has no --remove-path equivalent. RustRunner.setup appends [patch.crates-io] gix-config = { path = "/eval/workspace" } to oracle/Cargo.toml at run time, so the candidate crate -- not the published crate of the same name -- is what the oracle links against. The oracle therefore ships WITHOUT a [patch.crates-io] section; a duplicate section is a manifest parse error. oracle/Cargo.toml carries a comment saying so, to stop anyone 'fixing' the omission.

runner_contract.note: RustRunner._reported_to_id reads the suite from the crate segment of nextest's {crate}::{binary}${path}, so the two scored packages must be named exactly `atomic` and `integration`. `common` declares no #[test] and is invisible to discover(). Verified by calling RustRunner().discover() directly against the oracle: 78 + 41.
runner_contract.depends_on_annotation: 41/41 integration tests carry a `// DependsOn:` comment in the block immediately above their #[test], giving 100% coverage (floor 50%). Verified with RustRunner.dependencies(): 41 keys, 26 distinct atomic targets, 0 dangling. Values are bare function names, matching depends_on_above's parser.

image_requirements.note: No fixture files, no shell scripts, no git. Every fixture in the oracle is an inline string literal and no test touches the filesystem, a clock, or a process environment variable it did not inject itself. Source::storage_location is driven only through the caller-supplied env_var closure, which is part of the declared signature.

source_meta.src_loc_note: src/**/*.rs is 10202 lines over 44 files; the carve excludes src/file/includes/{mod,types}.rs (492 lines), leaving 9710. The oracle member crates are edition 2021, not 2024: editions are per-crate, nothing in the oracle needs a 2024 feature, and 2021 keeps the oracle off the candidate's rust-version 1.85 MSRV floor.

filter.expansion_note: 140 kept upstream functions became 92 oracle tests -- a net merge, not an expansion: upstream organises by which method is called, the oracle by which declared behaviour is asserted, so nine upstream files testing one rule from different entry points collapse to one test. One upstream function (read_only.rs::get_value_for_all_provided_values) was split five ways because each arm runs a different TryFrom<BString> impl. 27 further tests are spec-derived with no upstream ancestor. 92 + 27 = 119. Merge table and derivation in filter/rewrite_audit.md §0; per-test provenance in filter/candidate_filter_map.md §1-§2.

validation.reference_detail: Upstream gix-config 0.59.0 @ 227619ad src/ plus a Cargo.toml with the path = "../gix-*" deps stripped to mirror a candidate submission, mounted at /eval/workspace in spec2repo-rust:latest. atomic 78/78, integration 41/41, total 119/119 = 100%. Log oracle/gates/run_reference.log. One edit to the reference scaffold only, which must NOT be copied into the oracle: features = ["sha1"] was added to its gix-ref dependency because gix-hash 0.26.0 fails to compile standalone (16 errors; its Kind enum has zero variants unless sha1 or sha256 is on, so its own exhaustive matches do not typecheck). gix-ref reaches the reference solely through upstream's file/includes module, which the carve excludes, and Appendix A lists no gix-ref -- so requiring a candidate to declare a sha1 feature would be widening the spec through the build system.
validation.dummy_detail: spec/surface_stub -- every spec-declared item present, every body unimplemented!(). atomic 0/78, integration 0/41, with 119 individually reported `failed` outcomes and zero `ok` events. It BUILT first: `Compiling gix-config v0.59.0 (/eval/workspace)`, `Finished 'test' profile ... in 2.51s`, NO-RUN BUILD RC 0, and grep -c 'error\[E' over the log returns 0. Per-test outcomes can only come from the nextest libtest-json stream, which requires a successful build, so the stub compiled and then panicked 119 times -- a passed gate, not the carrier-block signal a build failure would be. Log oracle/gates/run_dummy.log.
validation.dummy_is_not_fairness_evidence: 0/119 is required but carries no fairness information on its own: a behaviour-free stub fails every test by construction, including an unfair one. The fairness load is carried by (a) the oracle COMPILING against spec/surface_stub, which mechanically proves no out-of-spec public symbol is named anywhere in oracle/**, because the stub contains exactly the spec's declared surface and nothing else, and (b) the reference run at 119/119. Six no_check hazards specific to Rust were enumerated before the gate was run rather than discovered by it -- size_of as a compile-time constant, iterator-returning accessors, derived Default/PartialEq on File/SectionId/Source, and #[should_panic] passing because unimplemented!() also panics -- and each was neutralised (filter/rewrite_audit.md §4). Q2, spec-derivability, rests on the per-row section citations in filter/candidate_filter_map.md and is the one gate here that is reading rather than measurement.

check_27_spec_surface_stub.sha256_recipe: find . -type f | sort | xargs sha256sum | sha256sum, run from spec/surface_stub; unchanged since S2 History #5, so the stub this gate linked against is byte-identical to the one check 26 diffed.
check_27_spec_surface_stub.build_provenance: ORACLE-LINKED, not standalone. The sha256 above comes from the same tree that run_gates.sh mounted at /eval/workspace for the dummy run, where RustRunner-style [patch.crates-io] gix-config = { path = "/eval/workspace" } repointed the oracle's dependency at it and BOTH suites were compiled: NO-RUN BUILD RC 0, `Compiling gix-config v0.59.0 (/eval/workspace)`, zero error[E lines. A standalone stub build would not have satisfied this check -- the divergences it exists to catch (missing methods, wrong derives, owned-vs-reference return types) are invisible until the oracle links against the stub.
check_27_spec_surface_stub.result: Zero unresolved symbols, zero arity errors, zero type mismatches across 78 atomic + 41 integration tests. No compile-stopper and no runtime-only spec gap found, so nothing needed repair before scoring.

evidence.cargo_lock_note: Cargo.lock was generated against spec/surface_stub (34 packages = Appendix A's dependency closure), not against the reference (91 packages), which still drags in gix-ref/gix-glob from the excluded includes module. Locking the larger graph would make the oracle demand crates the spec never asks a candidate for.

validation.count_reconciliation: The authoritative count is RustRunner._TEST_FN, which requires the #[test] attribute to be followed by an fn: 78 atomic + 41 integration = 119, agreeing element-for-element with the 119 case keys nextest reported in the reference run. Unlike the gix-ref carve, raw `grep -c '#\[test\]'` does not over-count here -- no doc comment in the oracle contains the literal -- so raw grep, line-anchored grep and the harness regex all return 78 / 41 / 0.

weaknesses: Mechanism 9. All 78 atomic tests share one compiled binary and all 41 integration tests share another, so a single signature divergence in a candidate is a compile error that zeroes the whole layer. The score gradient is therefore closer to binary than 119 tests suggests. Inherent to compiled languages; not fixable by test selection.

Q2 (spec-derivability) is unmeasured. The spec-section citation on each of the 119 rows in filter/candidate_filter_map.md is my reading, not a machine check. A behaviour I believe a section declares but that a careful candidate reader would not extract produces an unfair test that every gate here passes.

File equality is under-specified (D39). Upstream impls.rs:104's `while let` short-circuits on the shorter side, so `[a]
x=1
y=2` compares EQUAL to `[a]
x=1`. The spec states only a sufficient condition. No oracle test probes the ragged case -- asserting either answer would invent a rule -- so a candidate implementing strict equality and one copying upstream both pass.

The spec's internal header under-lists the source boundary (D40), and the S3A audit scanned the tree instead of trusting it. Two corrections: source_boundary says '12 carve test files' and PIPELINE_STATE History #7 says 18, but the true figure is 16 in-scope files of which 13 contain tests; and the src/ list omits eight files the carve's compiled surface needs (src/format.rs, src/file/access/mod.rs, src/parse/{comment,event,events,format,from_bytes/mod}.rs, src/parse/section/unvalidated.rs) -- src/format.rs backs the value escaping every declared setter relies on. The oracle is unaffected, but a candidate packet assembled from the header would be incomplete. spec/** is outside this task's write partition, so this is reported rather than fixed.

One upstream test was dropped for contradicting the spec rather than rewritten: write.rs::inserted_newlines_use_each_sections_newline_style asserts a per-section newline style, while spec L557-562 and L764 mandate the document's detected style for every insertion. AGENTS.md Rule 3 forbids widening the spec to admit it. Its spec-conformant sibling is kept, so newline detection is still covered, but per-section newline style is deliberately uncovered behaviour.
BodyRefIter's absence of derives (D38) is not testable through the public surface, and neither the oracle nor the spec differ can express 'this type derives nothing'.

write_to / write_to_filter I/O error propagation is uncovered. Section selection is tested; an io::Error path needs a failing writer, and the spec declares the propagation without declaring a way to observe it through the public surface.

Declared-surface divergences the second probe exposed: MultiValueMut::get and ValueMut::get return Option instead of the declared Result; ValueMut::set_string, delete and section absent; value_names collected into Vec<String> instead of the declared iterator; two undeclared IntoBStringOpt impls (Option<&BStr>, Option<&str>) made every bare None argument ambiguous.

integration_gap.measurement: two sigfix probes over two independent qwen3.8-max attempts on the same spec.
integration_gap.note: Both attempts land well below the 50% ceiling (43.7% and 37.0%) with the integration layer stuck at 5/41 in each. The classification is stable across samples rather than resting on one draw.

mutation_status.structural_cause: The oracle shapes that resist mutation -- parametrised classification arrays, round-trip identity assertions, computed metrics -- are fixed once the oracle is built. Selecting a mutation after the oracle exists does not work (AGENTS.md 6a).
